rejected_variants.reason: Rejected after real-map review because the repeated wraparound ledges read as a conspicuous corkscrew or sticker rather than ordinary geology.
rejected_variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: native adventure-map mountain sprite source
Input images: Image 1 is a style, palette, camera, and lighting reference only.
Primary request: Create a narrow diagonal hogback mountain column with offset stepped ledges and two unequal crowns, an uninterrupted geological landform for a single-cell-wide north-to-south impassable spine. Give it a broad lower foreground face and naturally tapered low left and right shoulders. It must read as connected mountain terrain, not a freestanding icon.
Style/medium: bright cartoony HoMM2-era storybook pixel art with crisp chunky pixel clusters, matching Image 1's charcoal, slate-grey, muted warm-grey rock and sparse olive lichen.
Composition/framing: centered isolated subject; high-oblique top-down, non-isometric camera south of the obstacle looking north; tall narrow silhouette roughly 1 unit wide by 2.4 units high; entire landform visible with generous padding; flat horizontal ground contact.
Lighting/mood: key light from map southeast/screen lower-right; right-facing planes bright, left-facing planes cool shadow; shadows fall northwest/upper-left.
Scene/backdrop: perfectly flat solid #ff00ff chroma-key background for local removal.
Constraints: one continuous opaque mountain subject; low self-terminating side extremes; crisp boundary; no transparent holes inside the mass; no cast shadow; no contact shadow; no floor plane; no text, UI, logo, or watermark; do not use #ff00ff in the subject.
Avoid: isometric diamond, conical peak, volcano, snow, trees, flowers, detached rocks, ground plate, scenery, horizon, gradients, texture, reflections, or lighting variation in the background.
